scientific_question: Does increasing chemically distinct reactive training reactions improve temporal localization when the event position is not fixed at the sequence midpoint?

data_policy.event_position_policy: SHA256-frozen random crop; no time, source index, projected_s, s_TS, or event position is supplied as model input
data_policy.primary_pair_selection: trajectory-gate-pass reactions; reactive pairs only; collision-free; max NVE drift <=0.01 eV
data_policy.nonreactive_TS_start_pairs: retained in Phase20C but excluded from primary training because they still contain TS-like frames and are not valid stable negatives
data_policy.stable_endpoint_negatives: not used in the reaction-count ablation; evaluate separately without changing the localization model

features.source: frozen five-seed B3v1 representations from C/N/O K-edge XAS
features.temporal_features: six scalar values plus their first differences

model.loss: balanced BCE + hard-negative ranking + 0.25*Gaussian listwise center + expected absolute delta-s

evaluation.fixed_validation: all 47 formula-disjoint official-validation reactions for every training prefix
evaluation.selector: global argmax of the three-seed mean probability after fixed 9-fs persistence smoothing
evaluation.primary_metric: reaction-macro probability that the selected frame satisfies |s-s_TS|<0.10
secondary_metrics: median absolute index error from closest-s frame

advance_rule: Report the full learning curve without selecting a favorable prefix; use the 617-reaction five-seed model as the final Phase20 detector.
test_policy: Official Transition1x test trajectories, labels, formulas, outcomes, and prior test metrics are not read during Phase20 training or validation.
